pronunciation.tip: Open your mouth wide: МАМА (mama) = mum.
МОЛОКО sounds like muh-lah-KOH (milk). Stress matters!

pronunciation.t: Р р is a rolled R
pronunciation.tip: Trill the tongue tip: ПРИВЕТ (privet) = hi.

pronunciation.t: Ы is a deep throaty I
pronunciation.tip: Say EE while pulling your tongue back: МЫ (my) = we.
Like the S in PLEASURE: ЖИЗНЬ (zheezn) = life.

alphabet.title: The Cyrillic alphabet
alphabet.explain: Russian uses Cyrillic letters. Many look like Latin letters but sound different — В sounds like V, Н like N, Р like R! Learn the sounds, not the look-alikes.

counting.title: Counting 0 to 100
rules: 40 (СОРОК) and 90 (ДЕВЯНОСТО) are rebels — memorise them! 21 = ДВАДЦАТЬ ОДИН (20 + 1).
counting.explain: Numbers 0–20 first, then tens to 100. Combine tens + ones: ДВАДЦАТЬ ОДИН = 21.

lessons.title: Greetings and names
lessons.learn: Start Russian! ЗДРАВСТВУЙТЕ (formal hello), ПРИВЕТ (hi), МЕНЯ ЗОВУТ + name = My name is... ВЫ = formal you, ТЫ = friend you. Start formal with adults!

grammar.title: Меня зовут + name
grammar.explain: МЕНЯ ЗОВУТ АННА = My name is Anna (literally: ME they-call Anna). Just add your name — no verb to change!
mistakes: Using ПРИВЕТ with a teacher — use ЗДРАВСТВУЙТЕ!
Saying МОЁ ИМЯ first — natives say МЕНЯ ЗОВУТ.

lessons.title: Буквы и звуки: русский алфавит
lessons.learn: Cyrillic has 33 letters: 10 vowels, 21 consonants and two signs that make no sound of their own. Five letters look Latin and are not: В is v, Н is n, Р is a rolled r, С is s, У is oo. The soft sign ь does not sound — it softens the consonant before it (мать, день). Stress is not marked in print, so it is learned with the word.

grammar.title: Буквы, которые обманывают
grammar.pattern: В = в · Н = н · Р = р · С = с · У = у · ь не звучит
grammar.explain: Read Cyrillic by sound, not by shape. В, Н, Р, С and У are the five that catch a beginner: вода is vah-DAH, нос is nohs, рыба is RIH-bah, сок is sohk, утро is OO-trah. The soft sign ь has no sound of its own; it makes the consonant before it soft, which is why мать ends in a soft t. Stress falls on one syllable per word and is not printed: молоко is mah-lah-KOH.

mistakes.why: Russian р is a trill, not the English r.

mistakes.right: В слове «день» буква ь не звучит, она смягчает н.
mistakes.why: ь marks softness; it is never pronounced.

dialogue.en: Thank you. And how is it read?
Smirnova, the stress is on the o.

lessons.title: Gender: он, она, оно
lessons.learn: Every Russian noun has a gender! -А/-Я = SHE (МАМА), consonant = HE (ДОМ), -О/-Е = IT (ОКНО). ОН/ОНА/ОНО = he/she/it. Spot the ending, know the gender!

grammar.title: Gender by ending: -а, consonant, -о
grammar.explain: МАМА ends in -А → SHE (ОНА). ДОМ ends in a consonant → HE (ОН). ОКНО ends in -О → IT (ОНО). ЭТО works for everything: ЭТО ДОМ = This is a house.

examples.en: This is mum. She is kind.
This is a house. It (he) is big.
This is a window. It is open.

mistakes: Saying ОН for МАМА — -A endings are always ONA!
Using ОНО for people — people are ОН or ОНА only.

lessons.title: Plurals and numbers in use
lessons.learn: Plurals are easy: add -Ы/-И! ДОМ → ДОМА (houses), МАМА → МАМЫ. Numbers agree: ОДИН ДОМ (m), ОДНА МАМА (f), ОДНО ОКНО (n). СКОЛЬКО? = How many?

grammar.title: Plurals with -ы/-и
grammar.explain: ДОМ → ДОМА, МАМА → МАМЫ, ОКНО → ОКНА. After К/Г/Х/Ж/Ш/Ч/Щ use -И: КНИГА → КНИГИ. ОДНА for feminine: ОДНА МАМА!
mistakes: Saying ОДИН МАМА — feminine needs ОДНА!
Adding -Ы after К: КНИГИ with -И, not -Ы!

lessons.title: Цвета и вещи: какой, какая, какое
lessons.learn: A colour is an adjective and must agree with the thing: красный дом, красная машина, красное окно, красные цветы. The question words agree in the same way — какой дом? какая машина? какое окно? какая is for feminine, -ое for neuter, -ые for plural. The ending is the agreement; the stem never changes.

grammar.title: Согласование: какой, какая, какое
grammar.explain: The adjective copies the gender and number of its noun. After к, г, х the ending is -ий, not -ый: синий, русский. The question must agree too — you ask какая машина?, not какой машина. Colour stands before the noun in the neutral order: белый снег, but снег белый also works when the colour is the news.

examples.en: What colour are your cups? — Blue.

dialogue.t: Синяя есть, а красная — только большая.
dialogue.r: SEE-nee-yah yehsty, ah KRAHS-nah-yah — TOHL-kah bahl-SHAH-yah.
dialogue.en: The blue one is available, but the red one only in large.
Then I'll take the blue one.

lessons.title: Моя семья и работа
lessons.learn: Two sentences carry a whole introduction: у меня есть + who, and я работаю + where. The profession stands in the nominative with no article — я врач, она инженер. Where you work takes в or на and the prepositional case: работаю в школе, работаю на заводе. The question is кто вы по профессии?

grammar.title: Кто вы по профессии?
grammar.pattern: у меня есть + кто · я работаю + где (в / на + prepositional) · я врач
grammar.explain: A profession needs no я есть: я врач, она учитель. To say where, working takes в for institutions (в школе, в банке) and на for factories, post offices and some sites (на заводе, на почте, на стройке). With a plural family, есть takes the nominative plural: у меня есть брат и сестра.

culture.text: An introduction in Russia carries three names, not one: имя (Anna), отчество (Ivanovna, from the father's name) and фамилия (Smirnova). The middle name is not optional in adult life — a teacher, an official or a doctor is addressed by имя and отчество (Анна Ивановна), никогда by the first name alone. The pronoun decides the distance: вы for anyone older or newer, ты only for friends, family and children. Getting this wrong sounds worse than any grammar mistake a beginner can make.

reading.text: Это Анна Ивановна. Она преподаватель. Её отчество — Ивановна, потому что её отца зовут Иван. Студенты говорят ей «здравствуйте» и называют её по имени и отчеству. Её подруга говорит ей «привет, Аня» — Аня это короткое имя. Один человек, три имени: Анна, Аня и Анна Ивановна.
reading.gloss: This is Anna Ivanovna. She is a teacher. Her patronymic is Ivanovna, because her father is called Ivan. The students say 'hello' to her and call her by her first name and patronymic. Her friend says 'hi, Anya' to her — Anya is the short name. One person, three names: Anna, Anya and Anna Ivanovna.

listening.script: Здравствуйте! Меня зовут Анна Ивановна. — Очень приятно. А вас? — Меня зовут Иван Петрович. — Извините, как ваше отчество? — Петрович.
listening.gloss: Hello! My name is Anna Ivanovna. — Very pleased to meet you. And you? — My name is Ivan Petrovich. — Excuse me, what is your patronymic? — Petrovich.

mistakes.why: A name with a patronymic asks for здравствуйте, not привет.
Меня зовут already contains the pronoun; я is never added.
The fixed frame is меня зовут, in the accusative.

task.title: Три имени
task.instructions: Write six lines of introduction between a student and a teacher: greet, give your имя and отчество, ask the other person's, answer, say очень приятно and take leave. Then read it aloud twice and check three things: вы everywhere, отчество built from the father's name with -ович / -овна, and no я after меня зовут.
